newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa returns home on a stretcher.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa returns home on a stretcher.

text.p: Lying on a stretcher with her eyes closed, Mother Teresa was released from hospital on Wednesday and taken back to her religious order after being given a clean bill of health.
The 86-year-old nun, who was taken to hospital last week after falling from a chair, was carried into the Missionaries of Charity order where nuns greeted her with applause, witnesses said.

"God bless you," Mother Teresa, her hands folded, said to Sister Frederica, the order's second-ranking nun, as she was carried from an ambulance into the order's headquarters, her home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta.
To the sound of the chapel bell, about 30 nuns surrounded Mother Teresa and sang and danced in joy before she was taken inside for a special prayer, witnesses said.

"We know she has a divine power and we prayed to God to make her stronger so that she can lead us in our work for the poor and the destitute for many more years," Sister Priscilla, a senior nun, told Reuters.
Later Mother Teresa, wearing her traditional white and blue-trimmed sari, was carried to her room where she was examined by a doctor, they said.
A doctor said Mother Teresa was carried on a stretcher because of longstanding back pain and not because of any lingering effects from the fall onto her head that she suffered on September 16.
"She kept her eyes closed possibly because of the glare of light," Sister Priscilla told Reuters. "For the past 10 days she was confined to intensive care."

"There is no cause for concern," said Dr A.K. Bardhan of Woodlands Nursing Home where she had undergone treatment. "Though she is alright, she is still very weak and she will be under observation for another 10 days."
He said a brain scan earlier on Wednesday showed a blood clot detected last week had disappeared.
Sister Priscilla said Mother Teresa was resting in bed. "We are very happy. We are grateful to God that she is back," she said.

The 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner has spent two stints in hospital in the past month. She spent nearly three weeks at Woodlands Nursing Home in late August and early September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
Less than two weeks after she returned to her religious order, Mother Teresa fell off a chair and hit her head.

A dozen beggars assembled outside Missionaries of Charity. "She (Mother Teresa) is like a god to us," said Mohammad Suleman, one of the beggers. "She has been feeding us for quite a long time. We are happy to see her back."
Children in nearby Nirmala Sishu Bhavan, a home for the destitute started by Mother Teresa, said they were happy she had been released.
"We prayed for her all these days and God has listend to our prayer," said eight-year-old Subhas Mondal. "She is our mother and she looks after us."
